title: new.target stays available: the host-authority rule refuses the import meta-property, not every meta-property
notes: The acceptance half of `the-import-meta-namespace-is-refused`, and the reason it is a separate case rather than a sentence in that one's notes: `import.meta` and `new.target` are the only two meta-properties in the language, they share a syntax node (`ts.SyntaxKind.MetaProperty`) and they differ only in a keyword token, so the cheapest wrong implementation of that refusal is one that refuses the NODE. That implementation passes the refusal case perfectly and is caught only here. `new.target` reads nothing from the host: ECMA-262 defines it entirely within the running function's own invocation, where `import.meta`'s properties are delegated to the host via HostGetImportMetaProperties — which is the criterion this area's forbidden list is built on, so the two land on opposite sides of it by the rule's own reasoning rather than by a table entry. Running it rather than merely compiling it is the point: `new.target === Tracked` is `true` only when the constructor really was reached through `new`, so a lowering that erased or rewrote the meta-property would compile and then print `false`, which no `diagnostics` expectation could see. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: any claim that `new.target` is CORRECT in every position — it is exercised in a constructor, the one position where the language has anything to say about it — and no claim about `import.meta` in an imported `.ts` module, which stays accepted on both backends and is recorded as unwritten in the refusal case's notes because it needs a support module this lane could not add. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared stdout line from `true` to `false` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 5cd2a507774e812d2ecc7c082f9941dc1561ec36ef3bb09fdb0bd6be9c5baf0b before and after). That mutation is precisely the wrong-lowering outcome described above, so the case is measured against the failure it is written for rather than against an arbitrary edit.
